title: Spaghetti Cacio e Pepe
subtitle: Pecorino, black pepper, pasta water
excerpt: Spaghetti in a sauce made from nothing but pecorino romano, toasted black pepper, and the pasta's starchy cooking water. Three ingredients; considerable skill in the execution.

recipe.sourceNotes: Cacio e pepe is a Roman pasta dish whose name means cheese and pepper. It is one of four classic Roman pasta sauces alongside carbonara, amatriciana, and gricia. The sauce is an emulsion of pecorino romano and starchy pasta water, no cream, no butter, no oil beyond what the cheese provides. The technique is everything.

recipeTools.notes: For cooking the pasta in a limited amount of water to concentrate starch.
For building the sauce, must be large enough to toss the pasta.

content.text: Cacio e pepe has three ingredients and one technique. Cook the pasta in less water than usual to build up the starch. Grate the pecorino to a very fine powder. When you add the cheese, take the pan off the heat first. If the pan is too hot, the cheese clumps into a rubbery lump rather than melting into a cream. The technique takes a little practice but the recipe is fast.

items.preparation: coarsely ground in a pestle or cracked

content.text: Bring 1.5 litres of water to a boil, less than you would normally use, to concentrate the starch. Salt it and cook the spaghetti. While it cooks, reserve a large mugful of the pasta water before draining.
Toast the coarsely ground pepper in a dry, wide frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute until fragrant. Add about 3 tablespoons of pasta water and let it bubble for 30 seconds.

Drain the spaghetti 1 to 2 minutes before the packet says it is done, it will finish in the pan. Add it to the pepper pan with another splash of pasta water. Toss constantly over low heat for 2 minutes.

Remove the pan from the heat. Mix the grated pecorino with 4 tablespoons of the hot pasta water to make a slurry, it should be thick and smooth. Pour the slurry over the pasta and toss vigorously, adding more pasta water a splash at a time, until you have a creamy, glossy sauce that coats every strand. Work quickly and keep tossing.
Serve immediately in warm bowls with an extra grind of black pepper over the top.
